name: Hand-Finger Anatomy Check
description: Validates hand and finger anatomy for correct digit count, proportions, and joint angles — a known weakness of AI generators.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated content by validating hand and finger anatomy against human anatomical constraints, exploiting the well-documented difficulty AI generators have with hands:

1. **Digit Count and Topology Validation**: The method uses hand pose estimation (MediaPipe Hands — 21 keypoints per hand) to detect hands and count fingers. Each detected hand is validated for: (a) exactly 5 digits present, (b) correct spatial ordering — thumb on the lateral side, pinky on the medial side, (c) no finger branching or merging (each finger is a single chain from palm to tip), (d) bilateral consistency — left and right hands should be mirror images. AI generators frequently produce hands with 4, 6, or 7 fingers, fused digits, fingers branching from incorrect positions, or two left hands. The method achieves digit counting through skeleton topology analysis — each finger must form a connected chain of 4 keypoints (MCP → PIP → DIP → tip) originating from the palm.

2. **Proportional Anatomy Validation**: Human fingers follow strict proportional relationships established in anthropometric studies: (a) finger length ratios — the middle finger is longest, index and ring are similar, pinky is shortest (relative lengths approximately 1:1.05:1.12:1.05:0.85), (b) phalangeal proportions — each finger's three phalanges approximate the golden ratio (distal:middle:proximal ≈ 1:1.6:2.6), (c) finger width decreases from base to tip with consistent taper, (d) thumb-to-finger length ratio is approximately 0.65–0.75 of index finger length. The method computes these ratios from estimated keypoint positions and flags deviations beyond 2σ of the anthropometric distribution. AI generators often produce fingers of incorrect relative lengths, inconsistent widths, or unrealistic thumb proportions.

3. **Joint Angle Biomechanical Validation**: Each finger joint has specific range-of-motion limits determined by skeletal and ligamentous anatomy: (a) MCP joints (knuckles) flex 0–90° and extend 0–30°, (b) PIP joints (middle joints) flex 0–110° and cannot hyperextend, (c) DIP joints (fingertip joints) flex 0–70° with minimal extension, (d) fingers cannot spread (abduct) more than 15–20° between adjacent digits. The method estimates 3D joint angles from the 2D keypoints using perspective projection and validates against biomechanical limits. AI generators frequently produce fingers bent at impossible angles — hyperextended middle joints, lateral bending at DIP joints, or fingers that curl through the palm.

4. **Temporal Hand Consistency in Video**: In video, the method tracks hand pose across frames and validates temporal consistency: (a) finger count should remain constant throughout the video (no appearing/disappearing digits), (b) joint angles should change smoothly — maximum joint angular velocity is approximately 500°/s for rapid grasping movements, (c) hand size should remain consistent (only changing with distance to camera), (d) skin texture and nail appearance should be stable across frames. AI-generated video often produces hands that change finger count between frames, exhibit teleporting digits, or show inconsistent hand geometry as the viewpoint changes.
parameters:
Hand detection: MediaPipe Hands (21 keypoints)
Digit count validation: topology analysis of skeleton graph
Finger length ratios: reference anthropometric distribution (mean ± 2σ)
Phalangeal ratio: golden ratio model (1:1.618:2.618)
Joint angle limits: MCP flex 0–90°, PIP flex 0–110°, DIP flex 0–70°
Abduction limit: 15–20° between adjacent digits
Temporal tracking: per-frame keypoint association
Maximum joint angular velocity: 500°/s
Minimum hand resolution: 64×64 pixels
accuracy: 83–92% accuracy detecting AI-generated hands. Digit count validation alone achieves 88% precision on StyleGAN/Midjourney outputs. Proportional anatomy validation provides AUC of 0.87. Joint angle validation achieves F1-score of 0.85. Temporal consistency in video adds 5–8% detection improvement. Performance is strongest for close-up hand views and decreases with distance and occlusion.
source: Farid, H. (2022). Creating, Using, Misusing, and Detecting Deep Fakes. Journal of Online Trust and Safety, 1(4), 1–33.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated images and video through hand anatomy validation. Supplementary signal when face analysis is inconclusive. Forensic analysis of full-body AI-generated content. Quality assessment of image generation models.
strengths:
• Targets the most well-known weakness of current AI generators
• Multiple independent anatomical checks provide robust detection
• Biomechanical constraints are absolute — violations are definitive
• Temporal tracking catches frame-to-frame hand instability in video
• Works for any image containing visible hands, not just faces
limitations:
• Improving generators (DALL-E 3, Midjourney v6) produce better hands
• Occluded or partially visible hands limit the analysis
• Small or distant hands lack sufficient resolution for detailed validation
• Unusual hand poses (ASL, musical instruments) have limited training data
• Medical conditions (syndactyly, polydactyly) may trigger false positives
